reviewer: control-transport.lisp:6 sets +fnn-control-io-seconds+ to 10, a fixed value. It is used for the reply send (control.lisp:126) and for the consumer deadline (control.lisp:708-713, which adds time only for waits). So the test at test_native_bounds_join.py:225 really does accept exit 3 for a large operator post that committed. The reporting is honest (uncertain, not wrong), so this is a product limitation the test faithfully records, not a test defect. It belongs as a design item (a time ceiling on the accepted/uncertain boundary), not as a correctness bug.
scenario: An operator posting any article whose commit takes over 10 s (large article, slow disk, busy owner) always gets exit 3 'uncertain' for a post that succeeded. The test accepts this as passing behaviour and treats it as settled, instead of flagging a fixed-time ceiling on the uncertain/accepted boundary (D27: bound work, not data). It also means the test cannot tell 'committed and reported accepted' from 'reply lost'.
title: The 10 MiB operator post is allowed to come back UNCERTAIN, codifying a fixed 10 s control deadline
